name: Birch extract
description: Birch extract , derived from Betula pendula, is a plant-based active used across cosmetic, nutraceutical, and food applications for its antioxidant and flavoring properties. It is commercially recognized under CAS 85940-29-0 and sourced from bark, leaves, or buds. Procurement teams typically evaluate it for active content standardization and botanical origin traceability. In personal care formulations, it functions as an antioxidant active in serums, toners, and scalp treatments where botanical positioning is a key driver. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a natural flavoring component, particularly in functional drinks and teas. It is ideal for health-oriented products where clean-label sourcing is a requirement for modern consumer markets. Nutraceutical formulators incorporate it into dietary supplements targeting antioxidant support. It is often used alongside other botanical extracts in capsule or liquid formats to enhance the overall efficacy of the final health product. Pharmaceutical and healthcare product developers also draw on standardized birch extract for inclusion in topical preparations. It is frequently utilized in herbal medicinal products that require high-quality botanical ingredients for therapeutic use. The material is supplied as a liquid extract, dry powder, or spray-dried powder. Solvent and carrier specifications vary by intended application, ensuring compatibility with different manufacturing processes and formulation requirements. Standard grades include cosmetic-grade and food-grade, with some suppliers offering specifications tied to marker compounds. These markers often include betulin or flavonoid content to ensure consistent potency across batches. Organic-certified material is available from select sources for clean-label and natural product markets.
